signals.evidence: Bokhris: 'If there's an alert, we leave everything in place and at most throw out the dough that's gone bad, clean everything and continue.' Workers at Afikim matzah bakery in Kiryat Shmona follow evacuation protocol during alerts.

Bokhris: 'They added us 15 seconds, so that's something' (smiling). 'The shelter is 10 seconds walk from here, so now we have at least another five seconds to get the matzahs out of the oven so they don't burn.'

Neam Wolf, sixth-generation manager of Afikim matzah factory: 'Each Passover is different events. This Passover, work under war and under missiles, three times a day workers go to the shelter. We worked here in the Six-Day War, Yom Kippur War, Gulf War, also in Corona with masks and capsules.'
Afikim matzah factory workers evacuate to shelters 1-3 times daily during alerts but continue production to supply matzahs to Jews across Israel and worldwide for Passover.
Daphna Ibtzcher: 'The truth is they were really cool. No one was hysterical, even my dogs are used to alerts. We made a big breakfast, drank wine because we're South Americans and that's what we do.'

Daphna Ibtzcher: 'I told them "you're already here, won't you tour Tel Aviv?" On Monday I took them to Tel Aviv, we did a tour of the Carmel market which was open so they could get a feel for Israel and then we went to Hostages Square and to a restaurant.'
During wartime, some residents report enjoying freedom from grooming routines (salon, gel nails, tanning, cosmetic procedures) and finding relief in not maintaining pre-war appearance standards.
Israel Railways limited passenger capacity on Jerusalem line to 1,200 per train in both directions on Passover intermediate days (April 3, 5, 6) per police directive for safety and security.

A 32-year-old IDF reservist and presidential award recipient, registered as organ donor, saved four lives through organ transplantation: lungs to 38-year-old woman at Sheba, liver to 71-year-old man at Hadassah, kidneys to 40-year-old and 64-year-old men.
Chief Economist's Office: Q1 2026 projected negative growth of -9.5% annually and -2.5% quarterly, reflecting severe economic damage since war outbreak.
Bank of Israel held interest rate at 4% and forecasts dramatic slowdown in private consumption due to war continuation, energy price spikes, and fuel price expected to exceed 8 shekels per liter.

Sara Netanyahu statement: 'At this time, when the State of Israel is in an existential war and in historic days against Iran, the lighting of the torch on Independence Day is befitting Israeli citizens who stand with courage on the front and rear.'
Viacheslav Vidment, police officer, did not shelter during alert shortly before midnight on Friday and was killed by shrapnel from interceptor missile explosion on road.

Gilad Ricklin, CEO of Egged Group: 'This means fewer trips on weekends, fewer at night, lower frequency. The meaning is that there are fewer drivers working, some on vacation, some with children at home and some who are afraid.'

Knesset approved unemployment benefits framework for 'Operation Shulamit' war: unemployed can receive benefits from day 10 of continuous absence from work; training period shortened from 18 to 6 months; benefits paid from day one without deduction.

Ayala Ben Harosh (57) from Nahariya: 'I immediately experience attacks of crying and trembling, the crying just doesn't stop. It changed my life, made it unbearable. Everything became heavy. When my husband is not home I live in the shelter. I also don't shower if there's no one in the house, and even then it's only a five-minute shower.'
Ayala Ben Harosh: 'When there's an alert, I feel a sensation as if I'm about to have a heart attack.' She was diagnosed with post-trauma after experiencing panic attacks during previous alerts.
Cohen family from Afula will celebrate Seder without father Raymond, who is serving reserve duty for the third Seder in 2.5 years. Older daughters will be at military base instead of family table.
Eliav Mayson, after 200+ days of reserve duty in Iron Swords war, called for fifth reserve rotation with Iran conflict outbreak; wife and children will celebrate Seder without him.
Ilanit Eliahu, at Hutzot HaMifraz shopping mall near Haifa refinery: 'It was a huge boom. Again heavy smoke, like last time. A lot of people ran to take cover. It was really scary.'
Second direct hit on Haifa refinery complex from Iranian missile in current war; damage to industrial building and 3,000-cubic-meter fuel tank; 13 fire and rescue teams deployed.

Atra, driver in 'Fourth Quarter' movement: 'We constantly reinforce the understanding that this is an important mission. Raymond and others beyond the Lebanon border understand how much Hezbollah threatens northern settlements. They see the danger to residents firsthand.'

Thousands of patients hospitalized in severe crowding in underground protected hospital wards since Iran war began; most wards are converted parking lots; conditions create problems: overcrowding, medical staff exhaustion, increased infection risk.

Teenagers from across Israel created digital community 'Another Shelter' (Memad Acher) on WhatsApp within hours of war outbreak, centralizing content and activities for protected space stays; hundreds of families joined within short time.

Northern border communities (Metula, Misgav Am, Matzuba, Kiryat Shmona) organizing public and private Seders in ~90 public shelters despite continuous fire; ~1,000 residents registered for municipal initiative; families self-organizing in groups of 10-60.

Segron, Kiryat Shmona official: 'There's a very strong community here. People are living the situation with courage - going shopping, sitting where possible, adapting to reality. Some choose to leave, and that's completely understandable, but those who stay, stay from strength.'

Sheba Hospital: TB patient hospitalized in underground ward for days near hundreds of other patients; ~750 patients exposed (including ~300 infants), ~1,900 medical staff exposed; preventive antibiotic treatment initiated for high-risk groups.

Church of the Holy Sepulchre approved for limited prayer services by Jerusalem police in coordination with Latin Patriarch, while Temple Mount and Western Wall prayer areas remain closed per Home Front Command guidelines.

Second direct hit on Haifa refinery complex in current war; multiple impact sites across city and nearby settlements; emergency responders deployed to multiple locations; no casualties reported but extensive damage.
Environment Protection Ministry: residents in the refinery area are requested to close windows in homes and not stay outside
Ramat Gan municipality launches 'Shelter in a Flash' emergency service: residents call a number, AI assistant 'Noa' locates nearest shelter and sends navigation link in real time
All public shelters in Ramat Gan have had wireless internet for two years as part of advance preparedness

Tzelir Foundation and Pais Lottery mobilize hundreds of protected hotel rooms for elderly and disabled residents from the confrontation line; funding, transport, daily support and community activities provided
Tnuva inaugurated new milk production line with 30 million shekel investment; eighth production line increases milk output by 15% ahead of Passover
Rabbi Zamir Isayev of Baku Sephardic community: 'Thank God, we feel peace, we feel safe'

Rabbi Zamir Isayev: 'The community's Passover shop operates as usual every day, distribution of matzos has already begun, and distribution of aid to needy families is expected in the coming days. Community institutions continue to operate in regular format'

Director of Ministry of Religious Services Yehuda Avidan: 'We see this as a supreme moral and Jewish duty. Our goal is clear: to turn hotels into a place of light and joy. Seders and Seder organizers are our expression of mutual responsibility and the resilience of the people of Israel'

Jewish Agency: over 20 million shekels distributed in four weeks — grants to damaged homes, emergency loans to businesses, support for lone soldiers; 2,000 new immigration files opened mainly from France, UK, USA

Jewish Agency subsidiary 'Amigur' protects approximately 7,000 elderly residents in care homes nationwide; teams reinforce shelters, distribute thousands of food baskets, coordinate physical rehabilitation of damaged buildings

Many businesses in the north approaching Passover on the brink of collapse: after Purim with minimal work, another month of partial or halted activity, and now Passover eve — one of the year's peak economic periods — business owners again confined to protected spaces without ability to operate

Tzelir Foundation and Pais Lottery announce transfer of hundreds of elderly and disabled residents from confrontation line to protected hotels; partnership adds approximately half a million shekels to the 'Banu' initiative
Resident Avi: 'Two containers for all of West Haifa is simply not enough. When the time comes everyone will go to the same points and it could become very dangerous'
Resident Miri: 'They ask us not to gather, but in practice they create crowding points. This is a contradictory and illogical message'
Resident Ron: 'This is beyond discomfort. This is a decision that could endanger people, especially when there is no protection available nearby'
Resident Liat: 'There is a feeling of unequal division here. Other areas received more, and for us it feels like neglect'

IDF identified missiles launched from Iran toward Israel; Home Front Command distributed advance warning directly to mobile phones in relevant areas; public instructed to enter protected spaces and remain until new directive

IDF spokesman announced defense policy of Home Front Command remains unchanged and will be in effect until Saturday night 20:00; restrictions and directives will apply during Passover and Seder night; Home Front Command continues to examine necessary adjustments in all areas, emphasizing education and gathering limits
Avihai Stern, mayor of Kiryat Shmona: 'From the dawn of history, wars were not waged against elderly, women and children. Why are we forcing them to stay here?'
Avihai Stern: 'We arrived at war without protection, so now we need to do everything to protect. Can't protect in real time? Get them out, simple as that'

On Yehuda HaLevi Street in Tel Aviv, where two Iranian missiles struck within less than a month killing two people, some residents decided to leave before rescue operations finished at the latest impact site; decision built gradually between alerts and impact sites over recent weeks

Private daycare centers collapsing: hundreds of working parents, soldiers on active duty and reserves left without childcare framework; operators demand property tax discounts, rent freeze on municipal properties, and additional aid

Innovation Authority survey of 637 Israeli hi-tech companies: 48% report significant employee absences, 71% report disruptions in capital raising, 87% experience delays in meeting development targets or product launches

75% of hi-tech companies report international flight restrictions impact operations; 35% report significant damage from inability to conduct business meetings, attend conferences, make sales, collaborate, and raise investments

76% of manufacturing hi-tech companies report production capacity damage; 24% report significant damage; 6% report complete production halt; 20% report significant delays in raw material imports; 8% report supply chain stoppage

Warning time extended to 15 seconds for all border settlements with Lebanon, but remains 'immediate' only in Kibbutz Avivim; after a month of massive Hezbollah fire, residents demand Home Front Command find ways to extend warning time there too

Noam Hillel, age 26, program participant: 'In the places where I fought — those I am now building. Once, when I passed through Sha'ar HaNegev junction, the harsh images from 7.10 would jump at me. Today I see green fields and what we built'

Yael Ringel: 'Our house was damaged in the previous round. We looked for where to settle and sleep peacefully without running to shelters every time. I didn't want to take the risk of leaving and seeing again everything we saw. We found a shelter that gives us what we need'

Yael Ringel: 'There is a kitchen, refrigerator, air conditioners and even a stage for children's talent shows. We have been living there for a month alongside more than 20 families who preferred the peace of mind'
Thirty percent of Kiryat Shmona residents decided not to return to the city after the previous evacuation; if another evacuation occurs, there will be nothing to return to

Israel Railways: during Passover intermediate days, passenger numbers on Jerusalem line limited to 1,200 per train per police directive due to operational complexity and need to maintain safety and security in mostly underground route

Chief Rabbi Yitzhak Yosef issued detailed Passover directives for wartime: if alert sounds during Kiddush, taste matzah briefly then go to shelter; if during Haggadah, stop mid-verse and go to shelter; if during Seder location change, no need to re-bless; continue eating 27 grams in reclining position when returning

Compensation Fund (Property Tax): 83 teams of surveyors and engineers operating nationwide since war start; 22,643 property damage claims filed: 14,825 for building damage, 2,203 for contents/equipment, 5,122 for vehicle damage, 493 for other damage

Family arrived after Passover with heavy debts; they struggled with severe economic hardship and reached Seder night with no money at all, forced to choose between basic products for children and important holiday items; they experienced a very difficult Seder night

Mother of four: 'The biggest pain is not hunger for food. The pain is seeing my children looking out the window at the neighbors' bags, knowing that this year our table will be missing - both the person we love and everything that symbolizes a holiday'

Second Authority Council extended permit for regional radio stations to broadcast on national frequency to provide accessible, continuous, reliable alerts and vital information to the public during emergency
Israel Railways announced passenger limit of 1,200 per train on Jerusalem line during Passover intermediate days due to security situation and operational complexity of underground route
Tzahar rabbinical organization launched free emergency Passover Haggadah adapted for wartime conditions, available on website and social media for those unable to conduct Seder properly
Soldiers' Association announced unprecedented support operation of approximately 10 million shekels for tens of thousands of soldiers and wounded hospitalized during Passover
Ministry of Health recommends public to contact HMO urgent care centers instead of emergency rooms for routine matters to preserve ER availability for complex acute cases and reduce hospital load
Ministry of Health issued urgent call for anyone exposed to infected tick in Kibbutz Degania B between 14.3.2026-28.3.2026 to contact health offices immediately for preventive treatment
During air raid alert in Bnei Brak on Saturday night, young people were watching missiles in the sky when a 15-year-old stabbed a 21-year-old with a knife, causing a 2-3 cm wound requiring stitches

Western Wall closed to public during entire Passover holiday; Jaffa and Dung gates closed; public transportation to Western Wall suspended; Priestly Blessing ceremony limited to 50 priests by advance registration only

Metula resident Yedidia Vangrover: 'We decided to celebrate at home in an intimate atmosphere. The Seder will take place near the shelter - ready to move immediately in case of alert. Despite the situation, synagogues became more active with residents gathering for prayers in shelters during prolonged stays at home'
Metula resident: 'We're tired of moving around. Many residents don't want evacuation. This time we expect the IDF to remove the threat at its root'

Gur Rebbe sent rare letter to Arad residents who were missile victims: 'We have seen great mercies, may God help you all merit the joy of the festival... through the power of Passover law, time is able to plant wholeness in the heart'

Sara Netanyahu declined torch-lighting honor, stating: 'The torch-lighting should be dedicated to the citizens of Israel standing with courage at the front and rear, to IDF soldiers and all security forces who defend Israel and demonstrate exceptional courage'
Ahvat Torah movement's Education Department launched daily one-hour Zoom sessions with thousands of children covering science and values topics in experiential format during wartime school closures

Approximately 20,000 new immigrants arrived in Israel since last Passover; 3,846 returning residents also came back, with majority choosing Tel Aviv, Jerusalem, Ra'anana, Haifa, and Netanya as settlement locations

Minister of Aliyah Ophir Sofer: 'Precisely now during wartime we witness the moving choice of thousands of Jews to immigrate to Israel and be part of our Zionist story. Immigration during war is a deep expression of Zionism, solidarity and faith in the righteousness of the path'

Second Authority Council extended permit for regional radio stations (Kol Chai, Kol Rama, A-Shams, Nas, Provia) to broadcast on national frequency to ensure broad, continuous, reliable access to Home Front Command alerts and vital information

League management issued directives: each team appointed officer responsible for Home Front Command guidelines; all stadium personnel must know protected areas; if alert sounds during match, referee stops play at natural break and directs players to protected areas

Kiryat Shmona youth department head Doron Shnaper: 'It will be hard to rehabilitate the department. When my child goes to the grocery store it's hell. We live from one protected space to another. Showers are like a military operation. Things I never thought about, the childhood I experienced this way is coming back to me now as a father'

Kiryat Shmona resident: 'We currently have 10,000 residents. I estimate that after the holiday more will leave. People don't want to spend the holiday in hell. Very loud, planes flying over us. We live inside a military base, except I've never seen a military base in Israel with children, women and elderly'
Sakhnin chairman announced team will host home matches at Ramat Gan stadium due to delay in installing protected spaces at Doha stadium, which has not met Home Front Command criteria

League A-C committee will recommend immediate closure of lower leagues; promoted teams will advance to higher divisions; relegated teams will be frozen; number of teams will expand due to many clubs lacking training facilities and protected spaces meeting security standards

Kiryat Shmona coach Avi Nagauker: 'We try with all our strength to preserve the children's spirit. Every day they receive a training program from me, near the protected space, at home, in the hallway, wherever possible while following guidelines. Players send me videos, fighting for their routine. We hope the military mission will be completed successfully and we return to safe and happy lives in our beloved city'

Opposition leader Yair Lapid: 'This has never happened in Knesset history. The coalition added hundreds of millions of shekels to ultra-Orthodox parties beyond budget framework! This is a pathetic gang of thieves disconnected from the people, robbing Israeli citizens while they're in shelters'

Officer in Battalion 941: 'There are many soldiers here giving their lives, and this is a harmful decision. There's no comfort in sending people home on Passover eve. They know how to pull you out when they want - and then they spit on you'

Approximately 30,000 children in Israel have lost a parent; 17,000 single parents raising them alone; over 900 additional children became orphans since October 7; unemployment benefits at 50-70% of salary create 25-50% income reduction for single-income families
Western Wall closed to public during Passover; Jaffa Gate and Dung Gate closed to vehicle and pedestrian traffic; public transportation to Western Wall suspended

Pais Factory and Tslir Foundation launching 'Banu' initiative to relocate elderly and disabled residents from confrontation line to safe hotels in Haifa and Tiberias with transportation, accompaniment, and daily support
Thousands of elderly and disabled residents in confrontation line communities unable to reach safe spaces during alerts; systemic gap in emergency response capacity for vulnerable populations
Eli Shraevi (hostage survivor): 'As a resident of the envelope, we experienced alerts for 20 years and a 15-second run to the safe room. Not something we're not used to - so I'm fine'

Rabbi Dr. Yafa Giser: 'There is a value system that has lost its moral compass, distorted idealism, unrestrained, in the name of love of the land... The majority is silent. There are entire settlements where people who speak out are not well-received'

Rabbi Dr. Yafa Giser: 'Silence this time is not neutral, it is complicity... There are those who oppose the phenomenon and are afraid to speak out. We must say honestly and painfully: silence is not possible this time'
Increase in burn cases among children and toddlers reported by Magen David Adom during pre-Passover period
Rabbi Beni Kalmanzon: 'I went from place to place in religious Zionism like Jeremiah and pleaded: stop with divisive statements... Polarization is a discourse of not listening to a person'
Alerts activated in Western Galilee following UAV; residents responded to alert system

Northern confrontation line residents face immediate shelter entry times (0-30 seconds) regardless of missile origin (Iran vs. Hezbollah); unified policy creates potential confusion during combined attacks from multiple sources
'City Shelter' initiative by Enav Center and Tel Aviv Municipality organizing underground cultural performances in public shelters during war to strengthen community and provide income to artists
Dozens of residents (ages 7-70) gathered in Tel Aviv public shelter to attend Yehali Sobol concert during war, finding cultural space within emergency shelter

Ministry of Health reports 6,088 casualties admitted to hospitals since start of Operation 'Roar of the Lion'; 110 currently hospitalized across severity levels; daily situation assessments conducted with Home Front Command

Ministry of Health directs public to community medical centers for non-urgent consultations; mental health support available 24/7 through Resilience Center (5486*) and HMO support lines; dedicated lines for northern residents in Hebrew, Arabic, Russian, English

Knesset approved emergency employment leave (Hel'T) framework for Operation 'Roar of the Lion': unemployment benefits begin on day 10 of continuous absence; training period reduced from 18 to 6 months; retroactive payment from day 1
Israeli Employment Service: 50,798 new job seekers registered since war start; 28,723 (56.5%) placed on unpaid leave; 12,731 (25%) dismissed; 205,824 total active job seekers; 63.4% women, 36.6% men
Ministry of Aliyah and Integration: 19,386 new immigrants arrived in Israel since Passover 2025 (April 20, 2025); 3,846 returning Israeli citizens; continued immigration despite ongoing war
Dr. Steve Katz: 'We arrived on Wednesday morning. The war broke out Saturday at around 8 a.m. That's when the first air raid siren hit.' The group was ushered into a bomb shelter.
Dr. Steve Katz: 'We weren't stuck. We were with our brothers.'
35 American participants engaged in volunteer and solidarity mission to support Israelis impacted by war, including resilience, therapy, and rebuilding initiatives in Israel's North and South.
Chef Shitrit: 'I was visiting Israel on February 28 when the first alert sounded, warning of an incoming Iranian missile attack.' It took more than a week for her to get a flight home.
Adeena Sussman: 'she keeps thinking about 2020 and the start of the COVID-19 epidemic' while sheltering in Tel Aviv with family and friends during missile attacks.
Industrial building and fuel tanker at Bazan oil refinery in Haifa hit by debris from intercepted missile; firefighters working to prevent fire from spreading and searching for trapped individuals.

Lior Latvik, Manpower Group Israel: 'This is a substantive delay and not merely a technical one, as it creates great uncertainty in the labor market, as employees and employers find themselves operating in a fog.'

Iron Sword Israel Volunteer Corp, a global volunteer network, mobilizing tens of thousands of people to support Israel on the ground and from abroad, dispatching volunteers to clean and restore homes damaged by missile strikes.
Growing number of Olim (new immigrants to Israel) volunteering to support reservist families and assist communities under strain, embedded in the country's culture of resilience.

David: 'We were able to resolve payment with the first place, so we looked around and booked a Passover program at a hotel in Europe. But then that one got canceled as well, probably because the Israelis who were signed up couldn't make it.'

Latin Patriarchate of Jerusalem and Custody of the Holy Land reached agreement with Israel Police: 'access for representatives of the Churches has been secured in order to conduct the liturgies and ceremonies and to preserve the ancient Easter traditions.'
Initial dispute between Israel Police and Church leaders over Palm Sunday prayers access at Church of the Holy Sepulchre during wartime, requiring presidential intervention to resolve.

Bank of Israel Governor Amir Yaron: 'However, even at this challenging time, the economy continues to show resilience, flexibility, and robustness, as has been the case for the past two and a half years as well.'
Aluma survey of 237 young people: only 30% optimistic about future; 64% report damage or freezing of academic plans due to war; 45% list education as primary concern.

Deluca, 39, arrived in Israel March 9, eight days after war began: 'My worry was, how could I get there as fast as possible?' and 'being physically present in Israel during such a crucial time was important to him.'
Deluca: 'Hearing about the soldier's sacrifice and watching Israelis rally around each other, Deluca was deeply moved.'
Protesters blocked Knesset entrance following state budget passage, demonstrating against government wartime policies and budget allocations.

Social Equality Ministry and IACC hosting public Seders for senior citizens; initiative to move elderly residents and people with disabilities from northern communities to protected hotels in Haifa and Tiberias ahead of Passover, projected to house more than 2,000 people.
Volunteers preparing communal Seders in hotels and providing daily assistance and social support to elderly residents unable to reliably reach protected spaces during alerts.

20-year-old Dallas native: 'My biggest fear throughout the whole war was getting stuck outside of the country rather than in the country. There was never a moment where I felt scared or something was going to happen to me. But rather, if I had to leave, what was going to happen then?'
Feinstein describing evacuation through Cairo: 'It's not a good feeling when you don't have the IDF behind you, and you're alone.'
Anti-war protests in Tel Aviv, Jerusalem, Haifa, and Beersheba with hundreds of participants, violating Home Front Command regulations banning events with more than 50 people; 21 arrested.
OneFamily nonprofit organized retreat for bereaved mothers of fallen soldiers and wounded soldiers, providing shared grief support and rehabilitation in Gilboa region.
IDF Chief of Staff suspended operational deployment of Netzah Israel battalion following detention of CNN crew; unit to undergo process to 'reinforce its professional and ethical foundations.'
Dozens of Arkia flights from Aqaba airport canceled due to Jordanian policy change; hundreds of Israelis stranded at airport.
IDF Chief Zamir: 'This is a serious ethical incident that does not align with IDF norms and values. We will not accept such conduct within the ranks of the IDF.'

Tzalir Fund and Mifal HaPais launched 'Banu' national emergency initiative relocating hundreds of elderly residents and people with disabilities from northern conflict zones to sheltered hotels; Mifal HaPais contributed 1 million shekels to expand scope to 300 additional evacuees.

Noam Wolf, fifth-generation manager of Matzot Aviv factory: 'Between one and three times a day, workers at the Matzot Aviv factory have left the production line, halted the machines and entered protected areas during air-raid sirens. But the disruptions have not stopped management from producing packages destined for Jews across Israel and around the world.'
Israel Police approved limited prayer framework at Church of the Holy Sepulchre to enable freedom of worship for all Christian denominations during wartime.
Shay Li, wounded soldier from Golani reconnaissance unit, told Defense Minister: 'We must not stop in Lebanon, it is really important.'

Families planning to return to evacuated community of Sa-Nur stayed overnight at site ahead of planned full return; group stated: 'The faith, determination of the families, and the support of the broader public make the path forward clear.'

Jonathan Davis, VP of Raphael Recanati International School: 'There are no classes on campus. All studies have moved online until Pesach in accordance with Home Front Command guidelines.' Students abroad continue via Zoom; exams postponed.
Jonathan Davis: 'I personally answer, at least while I'm awake, every email I get within minutes,' emphasizing policy of personal responsiveness to students and parents.

Tzohar Rabbinical Organization released guide of halachot for Passover in wartime, providing specific guidance on conducting Seder with possible siren interruptions, including which core components to prioritize and what to do during alerts.

Nova festival survivor Shaked: 'To think that on the Seder night I'll be eating matzot that we made ourselves, with our own hands, carefully following all the halachic rules-it gives this special commandment a completely different meaning. After everything we've been through, to hold such a matzah in my hand-something created out of desire and connection to our tradition - this is the real victory.'
